title: वीरेकी आमा कथामा जातीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा रमेश विकलको 'वीरेकी आमा’ कथामा आधारित भई वर्णवादी समाजको माथिल्लो जात मानिने ब्राह्मण र तल्लो जात मानिने दलितबिचको श्रेणीक्रममा आधारित जातीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध देखाइएको छ । यस कथामा तत्कालीन नेपाली समाजको वर्णाश्रमयुक्त व्यवस्थामा आधारित कथित उच्च जातीय आर्थिक सम्बन्ध र त्यसका आडमा कथित निम्न जातिमाथि गरिएको विभेदजन्य तथा उत्पीडनकारी जातीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । सर्वेक्षण, सूक्ष्म पठन तथा पाठविश्लेषणको विधि प्रयोग गरी समग्रमा विश्लेषणात्मक विधिमार्फत सामान्यीकृत निष्कर्ष प्रस्तुत गरिएको यस अध्ययनमा सांस्कृतिक अध्ययनअन्तर्गत जातीय शक्तिसम्बन्धको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । सीमान्तीकृत समुदायको निम्न जातको कमजोर आर्थिक अवस्था देखाइएको यस कथामा ग्रामीण जीवनका निम्न जातीय समुदायका पीडा, दुःख र जीवनसङ्घर्षको प्रस्तुति छ । यसमा तत्कालीन समाजमा सामन्तवादी विमर्शात्मक संरचना क्रियाशील रहेका कारण उत्पादनका साधनमाथि उच्च जातीयवर्गीय वर्चस्व कायम भएको छ र त्यसबाट निर्मित तथा प्रसारित ज्ञानका कारण जातीय शक्तिसम्बन्ध धमिलिई शत्रुतापूर्ण बनेको देखाइएको छ । तत्कालीन समाजमा उत्पादनका सबै साधनमाथि कथित उच्च जातको वर्चस्व रहेको हुनाले वितरण प्रणाली र सामाजिक प्रभुत्वमा पनि उच्च जात भनिएकाकै आधिपत्य स्थापित भएको देखाइएको यसमा जातीय विभेद, दमन र तत्कालीन समाजमा स्थापित सामन्ती ढाँचाको विमर्शात्मक संरचनाले कथित उच्च जातलाई शासक र निम्न जातलाई शासितको स्थान तय गरिदिएर वर्गीय दमन र शोषणका लागि आधार तयार पारेको देखाइएको छ । स्थानीय सत्तामा कथित उच्च जातकै वर्चस्व रहेको र केन्द्रीय सत्तासम्मको पहुँचसमेत उच्च जातकै भएका कारण श्रमको मूल्य निर्धारण, सामाजिक न्याय, श्रमको अतिरिक्त मूल्यको शोषण जस्ता कार्यमा कथित उच्च जातले छुट पाएको विषयवस्तु यस कथामा छ । तत्कालीन वर्णवादी समाजमा एउटा जातले अर्को जातमाथि गर्ने विभेद, शोषण, दमन र उत्पीडनको स्वरूपलाई निष्कर्षका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरिएको यस अध्ययनमा सामन्तवादी,पुँजीवादी, वर्णवादी समाज र सामाजिक संरचना भएकै कारणले त्यस बेलाको विमर्शात्मक संरचना नै निम्न जातमाथि सत्ता र शक्तिको पहुँचका कारण शोषण गर्न क्रियाशील थियो भन्ने निष्कर्ष प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In this article, based on Ramesh Vikal's story 'Vireki Aama', the caste power relation based on the hierarchy between the high caste regarded as Brahmin and the low caste regarded as Dalit in a varna-based society is shown. In this story, the so-called high-caste economic relation based on the varna-ashrama system of the then Nepali society and the discriminatory and oppressive caste power relation inflicted on the so-called lower castes under its cover are presented. In this study, which presents generalized conclusions through an overall analytical method using survey, close reading and textual analysis, caste power relations have been analyzed under cultural studies. In this story, which shows the weak economic condition of the lower caste of the marginalized community, there is a depiction of the pain, suffering and life-struggle of the lower-caste communities of rural life. In this, because a feudal discursive structure was active in the then society, high-caste class dominance was established over the means of production, and because of the knowledge constructed and disseminated from that, caste power relations became blurred and turned hostile, as is shown. In this, because the so-called high caste held dominance over all the means of production in the then society, dominance was also established by the so-called high caste in the distribution system and social supremacy; in this, caste discrimination, oppression, and the discursive structure of the feudal pattern established in the then society fixed the place of the so-called high caste as ruler and the lower caste as ruled, thereby preparing the ground for class oppression and exploitation, as is shown. In this story there is the subject matter that, because dominance of the so-called high caste existed in local power and access even to central power belonged to the high caste, the so-called high caste was exempted in matters such as determination of the value of labor, social justice and exploitation of surplus value of labor. In this study, which presents as conclusions the form of discrimination, exploitation, oppression and persecution that one caste inflicted upon another in the then varna-based society, the conclusion is presented that because society and social structure were feudal, capitalist and varna-based, the discursive structure of that time was itself active in exploiting the lower caste through access to power and authority.

australian_english: In this paper, drawing on Ramesh Vikal's story 'Vireki Aama', the caste power relation based on the hierarchy between the high caste taken to be Brahmin and the low caste taken to be Dalit in a varna-based society is shown. This story presents the so-called high-caste economic relation rooted in the varna-ashrama system of the then Nepali society and the discriminatory and oppressive caste power relation practised against the so-called lower castes under its shelter. In this study, which puts forward generalised conclusions through an overall analytical method using survey, close reading and textual analysis, caste power relations are examined within cultural studies. In this story, which depicts the weak economic condition of the lower caste of the marginalised community, rural life's lower-caste communities' pain, suffering and life-struggle are portrayed. In it, because a feudal discursive structure was at work in the then society, high-caste class dominance was set up over the means of production, and owing to the knowledge built and spread from that, caste power relations became muddied and hostile, as is shown. In it, because the so-called high caste dominated all the means of production in the then society, dominance was also set up by the so-called high caste in the distribution system and social supremacy; in it, caste discrimination, oppression, and the discursive structure of the feudal pattern established in the then society placed the so-called high caste as ruler and the lower caste as ruled, thereby preparing the ground for class oppression and exploitation, as is shown. This story contains the subject matter that, because the so-called high caste held sway in local power and access even to central power was the high caste's, the so-called high caste was given exemption in matters such as determination of the value of labour, social justice and exploitation of surplus value of labour. In this study, which presents as conclusions the form of discrimination, exploitation, oppression and persecution that one caste meted out to another in the then varna-based society, the conclusion is reached that because society and social structure were feudal, capitalist and varna-based, the discursive structure of that time was itself at work exploiting the lower caste through access to power and authority.
informal_english: This article looks at Ramesh Vikal's story 'Vireki Aama' to show the caste power setup between the high caste (Brahmin) and the low caste (Dalit) in a varna-based society. In the story, you see the so-called high-caste economic ties built on the varna-ashrama system of the Nepal of that time, and the discriminatory, oppressive caste power relations carried out against the so-called lower castes under that cover. The study uses survey, close reading and textual analysis overall to draw general conclusions, and looks at caste power relations under cultural studies. The story shows how weak the lower caste of the marginalized community's economic condition is, and portrays the pain, suffering and life-struggle of lower-caste folks in rural life. Because a feudal way of talking about things was running the show in that society, high-caste folks held sway over the means of production, and the knowledge that came out of that blurred caste power relations until they turned hostile. Since the so-called high caste dominated all the means of production back then, they dominated the distribution system and social pecking order too; the feudal setup of that time fixed the so-called high caste as rulers and the lower caste as ruled, laying the groundwork for class oppression and exploitation. Because the so-called high caste ran local power and had access even to central power, they got a free pass on things like setting the value of labor, social justice and exploiting surplus labor value - that's the subject matter of this story. The study presents as conclusions the discrimination, exploitation, oppression and persecution one caste dished out to another in that varna-based society, and concludes that because society and social structure were feudal, capitalist and varna-based, the discourse of that time was busy exploiting the lower caste through access to power and authority.
